display.title: Episode 344: The Storyteller, Chapter 7 (Before Rosh Hashanah)
display.summary_short: Chof-Hey Elul and the creation of the world, the Hakochainik march, the Baal Shem Tov summons a feared official, Shema with a first-grade class, and the blessing of the last Shabbos of the year.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 24 Elul 5748, days before Rosh Hashanah. Uncle Yossi explains that the world was created on the 25th of Elul, so Rosh Hashanah marks the sixth day, when Adam and Chavah were created to serve Hashem through the 613 mitzvos; as the Rebbe said, now is the time for simcha, which will bring Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march to 'Ki Imanu Keil', the story continues: the feared official Alex, surprisingly friendly, promises to visit the Baal Shem Tov that evening, but the Baal Shem Tov insists he come immediately, even if Rabbi Yehuda must lead him by the hand. A first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema. Alex comes, and alone by candlelight the Baal Shem Tov tells him, 'Listen, my child, listen carefully.' After a sponsor message, Uncle Yossi explains the Selichos days and why the last Shabbos of the year brings a blessing for the whole year, so everyone says Tehillim early that morning. He reminds listeners of Rosh Hashanah's dates, the shofar and Tashlich, announces the next show on Erev Yom Kippur, and wishes all a good and sweet year.
display.lesson: We were created to serve Hashem with Torah and mitzvos; prepare for the new year with teshuvah, Tehillim and simcha.

date.note: Confirmed in the audio: 'today is Chof-Daled Elul'; Rosh Hashanah on the following Monday and Tuesday.

advisories.note: A harsh official feared by the Jews of his town is summoned by the Baal Shem Tov.

privacy.note: A class of Shema guests introduce themselves by full name.

characters: Rabbi Yehuda, the Baal Shem Tov's shamash

sources_cited.note: Explained as the 248 positive and 365 negative mitzvos.
'Now is the time to be b'simcha', which will bring Moshiach.
Shabbos is the source of blessing for the days that follow.
The Baal Shem Tov's teaching that Hashem Himself blesses the month on the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah.
